newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil seen steady, Brent level to 5 cts up.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil seen steady, Brent level to 5 cts up.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures are expected to open around unchanged in line with a broadly neutral outlook for Brent crude futures, brokers said.
Brent is expected to open unchanged to five cents higher and move sideways in a two-week-old $17.65-$18.45 range barring any strong headlines, brokers said.
Front month August Brent settled at $17.85 a barrel on Thursday, down 37 cents on the day and three cents off the low. July gas oil settled at $161.75 a tonne.
The call was in line with the August contract on SIMEX, which was untraded and quoted at $17.85/95 in Singapore.

It also reflects a last trade of August WTI at $19.13 on the U.S. overnight ACCESS system, four cents above Thursday's close. The NYMEX contract slipped 43 cents on Thursday on doubts about OPEC quota adherence.
"An IPE broker said: "Technically some indicators are pushing up but there doesn't seem to be any momentum and the bias will be to the downside of the range."
Following the end of OPEC talks in Vienna the focus will settle once again on the timing of a resumption of Iraqi oil exports under the second 180-day period of the U.N. "oil-for-food" plan.
Thursday's slide was helped by doubts about OPEC's ability to stem chronic overproduction by forcing long-time quota-busters to adhere to quotas and buoy sagging prices.

Bears continue to derive momentum from a strong OPEC denial that Venezuela admitted overproducing at the group's six-monthly talks in Vienna. Brokers said any such admission would have been a constructive sign that members were working on a solution.
OPEC members currently pump out 2 million barrels per day above the agreed limit of 25.03 million bpd. OPEC oil ministers agreed on Thursday to freeze the figure for six months.
